theme.title: Mixed / Stock-Picker's Market
theme.summary: Consumer Discretionary (+4.67%) and Consumer Staples (+3.83%) led the market today, while Energy (-4.87%) and Industrials (-1.08%) brought up the rear. Performance didn't cluster cleanly by style — growth averaged +2.63%, defensives +2.49%, and value/cyclicals +0.44% — more a stock-by-stock market than a single broad theme. That shows up at the index level too: the blue-chip Dow gained +3.04% while the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell +1.97%, a wide enough gap to matter. Small caps underperformed as well, with the Russell 2000 at +1.47%, hinting the move favored large, established balance sheets over smaller, more rate-sensitive companies. The VIX fell 18.69% to 16.92, which reads as an orderly rotation rather than panic-driven selling. Gold added 2.63% to $4,070.80, crude oil was little changed at $88.07, and bitcoin gained 3.71% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
